takeaway: Extradural haemorrhage: the middle meningeal artery enters the skull through the foramen spinosum and lies in a groove on the temporal bone. A fracture here can tear it.

lines.text: A young footballer heads the ball, and he is knocked unconscious.
He is out for less than a minute, and then he carries on playing.
By the end of the game he is drowsy, and in the emergency department his Glasgow Coma Score is 13.
The CT scan shows an extradural haemorrhage.
Which vessel bled? The middle meningeal artery. It enters the skull through the foramen spinosum,
and it lies in a groove on the temporal bone.
So a fracture in this region can tear the artery and cause an extradural haemorrhage.
